title: Scalars and vectors: why direction matters
examples: What is the difference between a vector and a scalar?
Why are vectors drawn as arrows?

explain.say: Your friend calls: I parked 500 metres from the station. Can you find the car? Not yet! 500 metres in which direction? Some amounts need a direction too. Look at the left side first: scalars.

draw.text: Scalars and vectors: why direction matters

draw.verdict: A vector is a size with a direction

explain.say: A scalar is just a size, one number with a unit. Temperature, mass and speed are scalars. 30 degrees needs no direction. Can you think of another scalar?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A vector is a size with a direction

explain.say: Now the right side: vectors. A vector has a size and a direction. 500 metres north-east is a vector. So is a velocity like 60 kilometres an hour north, or a force pushing down.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A vector is a size with a direction

explain.say: That is why vectors are drawn as arrows. The length shows the size, and the way it points shows the direction. Look at the bottom of the right side. Is a speed of 60 kilometres an hour a vector?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A vector is a size with a direction

explain.say: No, it is a scalar, until you add a direction! Well done. Pilots, sailors and phone maps all work with vectors, because getting somewhere needs both how far and which way.

faq.q: What is the difference between a vector and a scalar?
faq.a: A scalar has only size, like 5 kilograms. A vector has size and direction, like 5 newtons pushing to the left.
No, speed is a scalar: just how fast. Velocity is the vector: how fast and in which direction.

faq.q: Why are vectors drawn as arrows?
faq.a: An arrow shows both things a vector has: its length shows the size and its direction shows which way.
asks: How do you draw a vector?

faq.q: What is the magnitude of a vector?
faq.a: The magnitude is the size, the length of the arrow. For a vector 3 across and 4 up, the magnitude is 5, by Pythagoras.

faq.q: How do you write a vector?
faq.a: In print it is often bold, like bold a. By hand you underline it or draw an arrow on top. It can also be written as a column of numbers.

facts: Velocity, displacement, force and acceleration are vectors; speed, distance, mass and temperature are scalars.
The vector 3 across and 4 up has magnitude 5.
